# waas.js — SDK conventions

This SDK is generated from the Palisade OpenAPI spec at
`openapi/palisade-api.json`. The architecture follows the blueprint laid out
in [`florent-uzio/waas.js#1`](https://github.com/florent-uzio/waas.js/issues/1)
(itself distilled from `florent-uzio/custody.js`).

## Types must come from the OpenAPI-generated file

All SDK types must be derived from `src/models/waas-types.ts`, which is
generated by `npm run generate:waas-types` from the OpenAPI spec at
`openapi/palisade-api.json`.

Reference the generated types via the two top-level exports:

- `operations["<operationId>"]["parameters"]["path" | "query"]` — request path and query param shapes
- `operations["<operationId>"]["requestBody"]["content"]["application/json"]` — request body shapes
- `operations["<operationId>"]["responses"][<status>]["content"]["application/json"]` — response shapes (when not already a named component)
- `components["schemas"]["<SchemaName>"]` — reusable response and body schemas

## Do not hand-author types that duplicate or conflict with the generated file

Hand-written interfaces or type aliases that mirror OpenAPI schemas are not
allowed — they drift from the API contract and make the SDK lie about what the
server actually accepts and returns.

**Never update or touch the OpenAPI spec file** — it comes from the vendor.

The only types that may be hand-authored are SDK-internal types that have no
API counterpart (for example, polling option bags, or unions composed from
existing generated types).

## Other conventions

- **NodeNext + ESM.** Always import with `.js` extensions, even from `.ts`
  files. No CJS shims.
- **Strict TS, no exceptions.** `strict`, `noUncheckedIndexedAccess`, and
  `verbatimModuleSyntax` are non-negotiable.
- **Thin namespaces over a typed transport.** Each REST resource gets a
  `createXxx(transport)` factory that returns a frozen object literal of
  typed methods. No classes per resource.
- **Single public entry point.** `Waas` composes namespaces in its
  constructor. Consumers only ever touch `client.<namespace>.<method>()`.
- **Errors are normalised.** Every HTTP error is rethrown as `WaasError`,
  carrying the API's `rpcStatus` payload and HTTP status code. Namespaces
  never see raw axios errors.
- **Naming.**
  - Files: `kebab-case` (`typed-transport.ts`, `waas-error.ts`).
  - Generated-type aliases: `Core_XxxYyy` (matches OpenAPI schema names).
  - SDK-only types: descriptive PascalCase (e.g. `WaasClientOptions`).
  - Test files: `<file>.test.ts` colocated next to the unit.
- **Use the `typeof-fns` helpers** (`isUndefined`, `isString`, `isObject`,
  …) instead of raw `=== undefined` / `typeof` checks.
- **Reuse pending changesets.** When making a follow-up change to an
  unreleased feature, extend the existing `.changeset/*.md` file rather than
  adding a new one.
- **Only test namespaces with non-trivial logic.** Simple `list`/`get`
  namespaces don't need test files.

## Regenerating types

```bash
npm run generate:waas-types
```

This runs `openapi-typescript ./openapi/palisade-api.json -o ./src/models/waas-types.ts`
and then `prettier --write` on the result. Never edit `src/models/waas-types.ts`
by hand — re-run the script instead.
